correctness.rationale: The assigned proof is correct. The coordinate-slice construction gives the upper bound. For the lower bound, finite truncation of the dual \(\ell_q\)-profile is legitimate for arbitrary index sets, coordinatewise Daugavet slices provide near-antipodal vectors, and the scaling lemma converts near distance two into the needed weighted lower bound. originality.rationale: A stronger published SCOPE finding predates the assigned record and mechanically implies it. That finding proves for every point \(z\) of an arbitrary finite or infinite \(\ell_p\)-sum of Daugavet spaces the exact formula \(\operatorname{dc}(z)=(\lVert z\rVert^p+(1+m)^p-m^p)^{1/p}\), where \(m\) is the infimum of the coordinate norms. Since \(\mathcal T^s(Z)=\inf_{z\in S_Z}\operatorname{dc}(z)\), and a sphere point supported on one coordinate has \(m=0\) while the formula is never below \(2^{1/p}\), the assigned equality follows immediately.

final_claim: If \(1<p<\infty\) and at least three nonzero real Daugavet spaces are summed in an arbitrary finite or infinite \(\ell_p\)-sum \(Z\), then the slice Daugavet thickness satisfies \(\mathcal T^s(Z)=2^{1/p}\).
limitations: The statement is mathematically correct; rejection is solely for decisive stronger prior coverage and consequent lack of independent value.
